gloss: to contain within; to encompass; to imply

definitions.gloss: to contain within; to encompass; to harbor; to carry inherently
definitions.explanation: To have something contained or embedded within as an inherent part, often something abstract like a problem, contradiction, or potential. More intellectual and abstract than physical containment.

examples.japanese: この{計画|けいかく}は{多|おお}くの{問題|もんだい}を{内包|ないほう}している。
examples.english: This plan contains many problems within it.

examples.japanese: {現代|げんだい}{社会|しゃかい}が{内包|ないほう}する{矛盾|むじゅん}。
examples.english: Contradictions that modern society harbors within itself.

examples.japanese: この{技術|ぎじゅつ}は{大|おお}きな{可能性|かのうせい}を{内包|ないほう}しているが、{同時|どうじ}にリスクも{抱|かか}えている。
examples.english: This technology harbors great potential, but at the same time carries risks.

notes:
A する-verb from {内包|ないほう}, composed of {内|ない} (inside) + {包|ほう} (to wrap, to contain). Used almost exclusively for abstract concepts — problems, contradictions, meanings, potential — rather than physical objects.

USAGE:
A formal, intellectual word common in academic writing, journalism, and critical analysis. Rarely used in casual conversation. In logic, {内包|ないほう} also has the technical meaning of "intension" (the set of attributes defining a concept), contrasting with {外延|がいえん} (extension).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {問題|もんだい}を{内包|ないほう}する — to harbor problems
- {矛盾|むじゅん}を{内包|ないほう}する — to contain contradictions
- {可能性|かのうせい}を{内包|ないほう}する — to hold potential within
- {危険性|きけんせい}を{内包|ないほう}する — to carry inherent danger

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {含|ふく}む — to contain, to include (everyday; broader usage)
- {孕|はら}む — to harbor, to be pregnant with (also abstract; literary)
- {抱|かか}える — to hold, to carry (more concrete; problems, debt, etc.)
